title: HexOct: The Laws of Stacking
description:
The Law gave the pieces, / The pieces prove the law. (DICTO)

Second edition, retitled HexOct, with The Laws of Stacking as subtitle (first edition: The Laws of Stacking, 28 October 2026, this record). A book gathering DICTO's work on close-packed stackings, from the Rule of Halves (#57) to spin ice and kagome magnets (#74) and the two tiles HexOct (#75): fifteen papers as a prologue and fourteen chapters in three parts, with a new opening, an epilogue and an index.

It shows six things. However equal balls are stacked in close-packed layers, the space is shared out into finitely many kinds of piece, each borrowed whole or in half from the cubic or the hexagonal stacking (the Rule of Halves). When a stacking changes, the pieces change only by swapping: the two mixed pieces add up to the two pure ones (the Swap Rule). For every piece fixed by its two neighbouring layers this is equivalent to the Hexagonality Law: every count and volume is a straight line in the share h of hexagonal layers. The counts that decide real chemistry and physics obey the law exactly in real crystals: hydrogen sites in metals (2 − h), faces shared in perovskites and battery cathodes (2h), eclipsed bonds in diamond, ice and semiconductors (h/2), kagome planes in magnets (1 + 3(1 − h)). Where a property depends on energy, the distance from the straight line is one number per material, sorting them from tin, on the line, to silicon carbide, far from it; in spin ice and water ice the loops that set the frozen-in entropy do not depend on the stacking through every length computed. Every close-packed stacking is a string of two layer tiles only, the c-tile and the h-tile (HexOct), built from the pieces of the Rule of Halves: any tile sits on any tile, flat where the walk weight is at most −7/24 and interlocking above. Part III adds HexOct-K, keyed HexOct tiles: keys on a layer's axis faces make it a Wang tiling, so HexOct-K layers can compute, shown by a four-tile layer that counts in binary.

Each chapter is its paper, theorems and proofs word for word, and names the paper and DICTO DOI it comes from; unrelated passages are cut; mentions of papers outside the book link to their DOIs. Sources checked for every chapter are listed in an appendix.

The ideas and names are DICTO's. Computation and proof with Claude (Anthropic). Licence CC BY-SA 4.0. More at dictospheres.com.
